messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
Here’s a concise overview of key Texas traffic laws (as of 2024). For detailed statutes, consult the Texas Transportation Code or official state resources.

| Area | Key Law / Statute | Practical Take‑away |
|------|-------------------|---------------------|
| **Seat Belt** | §545.021 – Seat belt requirement for all occupants of a passenger vehicle. | All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts; failure can result in a $50 fine plus points on your driver’s license. |
| **Child Safety Seats** | §545.023 – Children under 8 years must be secured in a child safety seat or booster. | Use appropriate restraints based on age/weight; improper use can lead to fines up to $200. |
| **Texting & Phone Use** | §545.051 – Handheld phone use while driving is prohibited. | Hands-free devices are allowed; using a handheld device can incur a $100 fine and points. |
| **Speed Limits** | §545.031 – Speed limits vary by road type; default is 55 mph on rural interstates unless posted otherwise. | Exceeding posted limits results in graduated penalties—$200+ per mph over limit plus points. |
| **DUI / DWI** | §545.041 – Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) limit is 0.08% for most drivers. | Penalties include fines ($500–$2,000), license suspension, mandatory alcohol education, and possible jail time. |
| **Driving Under Influence of Drugs** | §545.042 – Impaired driving with drugs is treated similarly to DUI. | Penalties mirror DUI but may involve drug testing and additional court orders. |
| **Reckless Driving** | §545.052 – Reckless driving defined as operating a vehicle with willful disregard for safety. | Conviction can lead to up to 1 year in county jail, fines up to $5,000, and license revocation. |
| **Distracted Driving** | §545.053 – Distraction includes activities that divert attention from driving. | Fines range from $200–$1,000 depending on severity and prior offenses. |
| **Parking & Stopping** | §545.061 – Parking regulations vary by municipality; generally no parking within 20 feet of a crosswalk or intersection. | Violations can result in ticket fines ($25–$150) and towing. |
| **Right‑of‑Way** | §545.062 – Rules for yielding at intersections, roundabouts, and when turning. | Failure to yield can cause points and liability for damages. |
| **School Bus Laws** | §545.063 – Vehicles must stop 20 feet before a school bus stopping to pick up/drop off children. | Ignoring this can lead to a $250 fine and points. |
| **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | §545.071 – Annual registration renewal required; vehicles must pass inspection if they’re older than 10 years. | Unregistered or uninspected vehicles can be impounded. |

### How to Stay Updated
- **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)** – Official site for registration, licensing, and rule changes.  
- **Texas Transportation Code** – Full legal text available online; check for amendments each year.  
- **Local County Courts** – For specific case law or recent rulings affecting local ordinances.

If you need more detail on a particular area (e.g., DUI penalties in Dallas vs. Houston), let me know!
